title: Spanish officer to Ottavio Piccolomini, camp in the Wetterau, 12 August 1646 (catalogue 2356): key rebuilt from the contemporary glosses of a sibling letter and tested on held-out cipher; inv. 25071 read in part

documents.shelfmark: SOA Zámrsk, Rodinný archiv Piccolominiů (Náchod), inv. č. 25071 (microfilm frame labelled "31/2")
documents.date: 12 August 1646 ("Del Campo a Ilenstatt [?] y 12 de Agosto 1646")
documents.route: Spanish-speaking officer signing "Joh: Behr [?] von ...", imperial camp in the Wetterau -> Ottavio Piccolomini

plaintext.source: Bare cipher: no gloss on the photograph. The same writer's letters inv. 25067 and 25069 (1646, same number table) carry a contemporary interlinear decipherment; they gave the key and the held-out test.

transcription.source: Vlnas 2017, appendix zip P_lohy_A_a_B.zip (theses.cz/id/p3p2kb), frame 25071.jpg: a photograph of the microfilm frame, rotated and soft
transcription.notes: Two passes from separate crops, reconciled on the image; pass 1 before the key was built, pass 2 after it was frozen. Independent blind check of 69 groups on 6 runs: 68 agree, 1 doubtful on the image (L09, 61 or 51), now marked doubtful.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution in two-figure groups, letters in alphabetical runs (20-64) plus a second run (10-24); code groups written apart: 67 Archiduque, 72 Principe de Darmstadt. No word division inside a run. The writer used an earlier, different table on inv. 25063 and 25065.
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the 49 tokens of key_frozen.tsv (47 letter groups, 2 code groups). Groups 34 and 56 are not attested by a gloss. length counts the 216 two-figure groups of the cipher lines (code groups included, plain script and gaps not counted); distinct 43, a doubtful group (30?, 61?, 50/56, 26/20) counted by its first reading.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary interlinear decipherments of the sibling letters inv. 25067 and 25069 on the same microfilm. Vlnas 2017 (theses.cz/id/p3p2kb) lists 25071 in appendix B as not deciphered. No edition found (catalogue checks 6 Nov 2026; repo checked 12 Nov 2026).

scripts in this folder (crops, mechanical decryption, mark check and word count, glossed-pair and held-out check)

solution.what: Appendix zip of Vlnas 2017 fetched once in Chrome; frames 25026, 25063-25071 (and 24852-24854) extracted.

Two tables found: 25063/25065 use an earlier one; 25067, 25069 and 25071 share a second one. Key of the second built from 32 glossed words and phrases of 25067 (pairs.tsv) and frozen in key_frozen.tsv.
Frozen key applied to 10 glossed words of the held-out sibling 25069: 9 letter for letter; one word has a group (93) not in the key. 62 of 63 groups agree. Small; the gloss was visible on the crops.
25071 transcribed twice from separate crops (pass 1 before the key) and reconciled on the image.

25071 decrypted with the frozen key and read with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes. Dan's reading checker on the Spanish running text: clean share 0.688 (11 of 16 sentences; the misses are period spellings).

Independent blind review by a separate AI language-model agent: own crops, 69 groups on 6 runs copied before the transcription was opened (68 agree, 1 doubtful: L09 61/51); decryption rebuilt; reading checked as sentences against the translation (16 of 16 hold). State read in part agreed, grade B.
L09 group 61 marked doubtful (61?) after the review; 'desarmarse' now counted as a doubtful word: 38 of 42 verbatim (90.5%).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 216 tokens, 43 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.258 per letter; random keys -4.687 (z 8.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.731 (mean -2.779, z 8.8); annealer on the real text -2.442. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.258; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.442

outcome.method_basis: Key built from the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the sibling letter 25067 (same writer, same table, 1646), frozen and tested on the held-out glossed sibling 25069, then applied unchanged to the bare letter 25071.

texts.label: inv. 25071, camp at Ilenstatt [?], 12 August 1646
texts.summary: The army has no intention of seeking out the enemy or risking battle unless the enemy attacks Giessen, which would have to be relieved: the Prince of Darmstadt must not be abandoned, if only for the common interest. Turenne has joined the Swedes, who on Queen Christina's orders demanded that the Prince declare himself and disarm or be attacked; he refused and said he would defend himself. The writer reports this today to the Archduke, who has promised to relieve the Prince in any case.
texts.note: Words 42: 38 verbatim from the signs (90.5%), 2 with a doubtful sign (aquel, a figure under an ink blot; desarmarse, group 61 of doubtful shape, possibly 51), 2 with a marked repair (cath{+e}gorica, o{u/y}), no guesses, no holes. Without the 3 code groups 35 of 39 (89.7%).

reading_review.note: Read as Spanish sentences against the English translation: all 16 sentences of the running text hold, and the 42 cipher words follow mechanically from transcription and frozen key, with two marked repairs (cathegorica, oy) and one doubtful sign under a blot (aquel). A blind sign check of 69 groups on 6 runs agreed on 68, with one doubtful group (L09 61/51, desarmarse, now marked doubtful); grade B, not A, because three words rest on a doubtful sign or an inferred value and the held-out test is small.

gaps.detail: One figure under an ink blot; one group 61 or 51 (s or u); one figure 0 or 6. A clean scan from SOA Zámrsk would settle all three.
34 (g, 'Giesen') from the table order and the sense; 56 (y) from context on 25067_1. The worked glossed text has no gloss for them; the further glossed pages 25067_2 and 25069_1 were not worked.
10 words of 25069 with the gloss visible; group 93 there is not in the key.

Date line reads 'Del Campo a Ilenstatt', probably Ilbenstadt (Wetterau), not Frankenthal as the catalogue has it; the signature 'Joh: Behr [?] von ...' is not read and needs a clean image. The slug frankenthal1646 follows the catalogue.
